messages.subject: Tinn-R problem
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I've been using Tinn-R as my R-script editor. While sending scripts
from Tinn-R to R, Tinn-R provides two ways to connect to R. One is the
R-term embedded in Tinn-R window. The other is Rgui independent
console window.

My question is: while i can send lines of script from tinn-R to the
embedded R-term, I CAN"T send them to the independent Rgui console?

Any thoughts on that?

my pc system: windowsXPpro SP3, tinn-R2.2.0.2 , R2.7.2

Thanks for your help!

Alvin

messages.subject: Re: [CorpLing with R] Tinn-R problem
messages.body_plain:
Hey Alvin,

I don't know if I understood your question, but I
think you can send lines into the RConsole the same way you do it for
the R-Term:
Highlight the line, hit the R menu, then SEND, then line (the point-click way).

If you have BOTH RConsole and R-Term open, the line will go to the
R-Term window. If you only have RConsole open (thru Tinn-R) the line
will go straight to the console.

Did I get this right? Is that what you're trying to do?

A.

messages.subject: Re: Model checking
messages.body_plain:
Hi Daniel,

I very much agree with you that Crawley's descriptions are not the
most informative in this respect. The best way to learn how to
interpret such plots and to identify problems is to make lots of
plots.

I recommend you take a look at Julian Faraway's "Linear Models with
R" (Chapman & Hall/CRC: 2005), especially pages 53--56 in chapter 4
("Diagnostics"). There you will find R code to make artifical plots
with constant and non-constant variance, non-linearities etc. (i.e.
plots with known properties). After looking at a few plots you'll
start to get the feel for how the various problems manifest
themselves. I also recommend the follow-up "Extending the Linear Model
with R" which deals with GLMs, mixed effects etc. However, the model
checking procedure is essentially similar for ordinary least squares
regression and various types of GLMs (Poisson, binomial, negative
binomial, Gamma etc.): the residuals vs. fitted plot should not show
signs of non-linearities or non-constant variance.

Best regards,

Gard

<danpire...@googlemail.com> wrote:
> # sorry for double posting
>
> Hi everybody
> ,
> I was wondering if anyone has come across a decent description of the
> model checking process in R.
>
> I am trying to fit a Poisson Generalized Linear Model for Count Data
> and am still rather inexperienced with these things (and I guess GLMs
> in general). When asked to plot a given model, R outputs a series of
> four graphs (residuals x fitted, QQ, ...). Now, I find these plots
> rather hard to interpret. The most thorough discussion I know of how
> these things should look like is Crawley 2007 (The R book), but the
> comments there are a little "impressionistic" at times ("This plot
> should look like a sky at night” Crawley 2007:357;  "[nonconstancy of
> variance] shows up as a triangular scatter (like a wedge of cheese)”
> Crawley 2007:359...).
>
> To put it bluntly: I am having trouble deciding if what I see is
> sufficiently similar to a sky at night or a wedge of cheese...;) Any
> hint as to where I can find a model answer for (Poisson Generalized
> Linear) Model checking and the interpretation of those plots would be
> tremendously appreciated.
>
> best,
> daniel

messages.subject: Notepad++ for R ....problem
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

As the new version of Tinn-R has given me quite a headache, I now find
more comfort in Notepad++ for R. Everything works well except one
thing!

As now I'm using NppToR to send all the r srcipts from Notepad++ to R-
console (using F8), all the scripts are passed through very nicely.
But if the command lines contain any "chinese character" string, they
fail to show up correctly on the R-console.

For instance, if i write in Notepad++:

which(original.rownames == "個");

and pass this line to R-console using F8, then on the -Rconsole it
becomes:

which(original.rownames == "?");

But the weird thing is that if I copy paste the script line from
Notepad++ to R-console, they work perfectly again.....

So, would anyone happen to know the reason??

My system: English windowsXP SP3, R 2.7.3, Notepad++ 5.5.1

Million thanks in advance!

Alvin
